notes:
POC summary: validate Dedicated capacity for high-throughput reranking workload while keeping chat p50 < 100ms and p95 < 250-300ms under production mix. Customer wants explicit throughput guarantees and a plan for reserved GPUs + burst autoscale for seasonal peaks.

Recent timeline:
- 2025-01-20: Kickoff call (Jordan, Priya, CTO Aaron Li). Recorded FF ff-84392. Confirmed scope: reranking + chat + embeddings.
- 2025-01-25: Baseline load test (internal harness v1). Setup: 4xH100-equivalent hardware sim. Profile: 70% reranking, 20% chat, 10% embeddings. Result: 280 rps @ 256 tokens avg, p50=68ms, p95=320ms (cache cold/warm mix).
- 2025-01-28: Tuning pass with Redwood SE: enabled KV prefix caching + continuous batching adjustments. Observed p95 drop to ~240ms on same load.
- 2025-01-30: Soak test started (target 72h). 24h checkpoint: stable throughput, no OOMs, GPU util ~68-75%, tail spikes when sequence length >1024 tokens.
- 2025-02-01: Architecture session: discussed reserved capacity shapes. Customer prefers deterministic pricing; leaning toward 6xH100 with autoscale burst to 8 during nightly peak windows. Redwood suggested A100-80GB profile for model variants with bigger KV usage.

POC test plan (approved in call):
- Load tests: progressive ramp to 400 rps for reranking (512-token tail), sustained 12h at target.
- Soak: 72-hour steady-state run at 80% peak load + scheduled spike windows to validate autoscale and graceful fallback.
- Failover: induce instance restart and network blips to validate fallback to compatible model variant (lower-precision) and traffic routing.
- Metrics: token/sec, requests/sec, p50/p90/p95 latency, GPU memory pressure, KV cache hit ratio, costs per 1M tokens.

Representative prompt samples used in tests:
- "Optimize route for batch of 120 orders given current fleet — response length ~180 tokens" (reranking/scoring mix).
- "Summarize last 10 customer messages and propose single action" (chat assistant, ~120 tokens).
- "Embed SKU title + description for similarity search" (embeddings, 64-128 tokens).

Security & compliance:
- Security questionnaire mostly complete; they require KMS/HSM attestation and SSO/SAML integration before production cutover. Data residency requirement: logs retained in NA region only.

SLA / commercial notes:
- Customer quote: "We need a hard p95 SLA or we can't replace our current on-prem cluster." CTO emphasized penalty-sensitive language for tail latency.
- Wants committed throughput (tokens/sec) and a clear escalation path for incidents. Requesting example SLA language and remediation credits.

Initial performance observations & asks for Redwood:
- Warm-cache p95 is within tolerance after batching/caching, but cold-cache (first-token after long inactivity) still shows spikes. Ask: recommendations on pre-warming strategies and persistent KV cache sizing.
- Cost sensitivity: wants tradeoff analysis for 6xH100 vs 8xA100-80GB (performance + unit cost + expected token cost delta).
- Need a short runbook for provider failover and autoscale triggers for on-call SREs.

Next steps (short):
1) Complete remaining 72h soak (in-progress).
2) Redwood to deliver written SLA draft + cost model for the two reserved shapes (due 2025-02-06).
3) Security team to schedule KMS attestation call w/ Redwood security (blocked until available).
4) Finance to decide on ARR band after cost model.
